GenAI systems flip this paradigm on its head. Their outputs are probabilistic, meaning the same prompt might produce five different answers if you run it five times. \u003c/span\u003e\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cblockquote\u003e“It’s a non-stable exploit. A prompt injection may work once, fail the next three times, and then succeed again under slight wording tweaks. \u0026nbsp;\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan style=\"color: rgb(14, 16, 26);\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFuzzing becomes fuzzier\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan style=\"color: rgb(14, 16, 26);\"\u003e. Traditional fuzzing relies on predictable system behavior to spot breakage. In GenAI, input variation is baked into normal operation, making it harder to tell signal from noise. \u0026nbsp;\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan style=\"color: rgb(14, 16, 26);\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAttack detection is harder.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan style=\"color: rgb(14, 16, 26);\"\u003e Because exploits don’t always fire reliably, security teams may incorrectly mark them as benign or false positives during automated scans.\u0026nbsp;\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003cspan style=\"color: rgb(14, 16, 26);\"\u003eIn essence, you’re testing a system that moves the target while you aim—so you need a new kind of patience, creativity, and persistence to uncover real threats. \u003c/span\u003e\u0026nbsp;\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3\u003eAI Outputs Are Attack Surfaces\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eIn traditional apps, outputs are a reflection of internal state. In GenAI, the output \u003cem\u003eis\u003c/em\u003e the system behavior.
